items.stem: You removed a running container that had written files to its writable layer. What happens to those files?

options.text: They are lost unless they were stored in a volume or bind mount
options.rationale: Correct: the container writable layer is discarded on removal; durable data needs a volume.

options.text: They are automatically committed to the base image
options.rationale: Removing a container does not alter the image.

options.text: They move to the host home directory
options.rationale: Nothing is relocated to the host unless a mount was used.

options.text: They are pushed to the registry
options.rationale: Removal does not push anything to a registry.

items.explanation: Correct: the container writable layer is discarded on removal; durable data needs a volume.

items.stem: What is the main benefit of a multi-stage Docker build?

options.text: Build artifacts are produced in one stage and only the needed output is copied into a small final image
options.rationale: Correct: multi-stage builds keep build tooling out of the final image, shrinking it.

options.text: It lets a container run as root more safely
options.rationale: Multi-stage builds are about image contents, not privilege.

options.text: It removes the need for a registry
options.rationale: Registries are still used to store and share images.
Multi-stage builds still use layer caching.

items.explanation: Correct: multi-stage builds keep build tooling out of the final image, shrinking it.

items.stem: Which TWO practices improve Docker image security or size? (Select TWO)

options.text: Running the container process as a non-root user
options.rationale: Correct: dropping root limits the blast radius of a compromise.

options.text: Using a minimal base image and multi-stage builds
options.rationale: Correct: smaller images reduce attack surface and size.

options.text: Embedding long-lived secrets directly in image layers
options.rationale: Secrets in layers persist and leak with the image.

options.text: Always running the latest tag without pinning
options.rationale: Unpinned tags make builds unpredictable and can pull vulnerable images.

items.explanation: Correct: dropping root limits the blast radius of a compromise.; Correct: smaller images reduce attack surface and size.
